summary: Full backend + focused frontend testing on Buddilio. Backend pytest suite: 34 tests, 33 passing (97%). Frontend UI: auth (all 3 roles), events listing, protected route redirects, role gating (user->/admin redirects to /dashboard), passes -> checkout -> coupon BUDDY20 -> pay-failure (402) -> pay-success (order marked paid + navigates to /orders), partner login lands on /partner, admin dashboard shows all 14 tabs + stats + charts, mobile /events renders. Registration validation (under-21, missing terms) rejected server-side with clear messages. Discover, messaging, partner event creation + admin approval, refund, plans CRUD, audit logs all working via API.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout is ineffective behind the k8s ingress. `identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}"` reads the direct socket peer, which is the internal ingress/proxy pod IP and rotates per request. In the test 6 consecutive wrong-password attempts from the public URL all returned 401 with no 429. Fix: read the real client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` header (first value), or key rate-limit by email only, and consider adding a global email-only counter as a fallback.

CORS is configured with allow_origins='*' AND allow_credentials=True. Starlette will drop credentials with wildcard origins, so cookie-based auth from a browser on a different origin will silently fail. Frontend currently works because it sends the Authorization: Bearer header, but the httpOnly cookie flow is effectively broken cross-origin. Set CORS_ORIGINS to the explicit frontend origin.
No password strength or mobile format validation beyond min_length=6; role is user-controllable in payload (can self-register as 'partner'). Consider gating partner signups to an approval flow.

issues: Member cards on /discover have no per-card data-testid (e.g. discover-card-{id}) which makes automated testing brittle. Interior action buttons (profile-message-btn, profile-connect-btn) exist on the public profile page only.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout: use X-Forwarded-For (or email-only identifier) so 5+ failed logins from the internet actually trigger 429.
Set CORS_ORIGINS to the explicit frontend origin (currently '*') because allow_credentials=True + wildcard is silently non-functional for cookies.
Consider restricting role='partner' at registration to an admin-approval step; today anyone can self-register as a partner.
(Nice-to-have) Add data-testid="discover-card-{id}" on each member card in /discover for test stability.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1216 lines in one file — split into routers (auth, events, commerce, admin, messaging) for maintainability.
login_attempts identifier uses request.client.host which is the ingress pod IP behind a proxy → rate limiting bypassed.
CORS: allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True is invalid per spec; browsers ignore credentials in this config.
Register endpoint accepts role from client-supplied payload — potential privilege issue for 'partner' role self-onboarding.

Some admin CRUD endpoints (crud_routes) use the same function name `create/listing/update/delete` in a loop closure — Starlette route names collide unless explicitly overridden (the code does override with `name=...`, which is good; leave as is).
seed_data_creation: Tests create ephemeral TEST_-prefixed users, plans, events, orders but do not delete on teardown. Non-destructive to seed. Also purchased a membership plan for aarav.mehta@example.com so his /membership is now active — kept intentionally to prove the paid flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py is the regression suite; run with `export $(grep -v '^#' /app/frontend/.env | xargs) && pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`. Note: pytest.ini pins -n 2 --dist loadscope, do NOT pass -p no:xdist. The brute-force lockout test currently PASSES only because we assert 429 appears; if main agent fixes the header extraction, it'll continue to pass. If they change identifier scheme, adjust accordingly. UI flows verified end-to-end: login (user/partner/admin), passes checkout with BUDDY20 + pay-success/failure, protected route redirection, mobile /events render at 390px.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout RCA: FastAPI's request.client.host is the socket peer address. In a k8s cluster behind an nginx/traefik ingress the peer is the ingress pod's cluster IP, which can be one of several proxy pods and therefore varies from request to request. Because identifier = ip + email, each retry effectively creates a new record with count=1 and never reaches the >=5 lockout threshold. Reproduction: `for i in 1..6; do curl -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -d '{"email":"x@x","password":"bad"}'; done` all return 401. Mitigation: parse the first entry of the X-Forwarded-For request header (fallback to request.client.host), or drop the IP portion and rate-limit strictly per email (with a global counter to prevent DOS).
